record.tranche_reason: The study compares model architecture variants and reports their losses, but does not fit or reproduce the original scaling-law measurements.
record.gate_note: The study reports a fixed-parameter-count depth/width comparison and a normalization comparison with loss outcomes. It does not report power-law fits, small-run loss predictions, compute-optimal parameter/token allocations, or loss curves across scale. Scaling-law results and claims from cited work are not rows. The 13.7% theoretical compute reduction and 15% increase in tokens processed for the shallow-wide model are efficiency outcomes, not loss measurements.
record.test_reason: Within a technical report, one ablation compares a 26-layer and an 18-layer wider 3B model at equal parameter count and reports validation perplexity. That bears directly on V4. Nothing else in the paper measures loss scaling, extrapolation, allocation, or downstream prediction against scale or loss.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase of the two ablations is accurate. The paper's overall conclusion is broader: HyperCLOVA X THINK achieves competitive Korea-centric benchmark performance at much lower training compute, with robust bilingual consistency and a strong vision-augmented variant. The scaling-law material is only cited.
record.recipe_differences: This is an architecture and normalization comparison, not a reproduction of the original scaling-law fitting or compute-optimal allocation procedures.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported loss outcome differs with normalization choice (Pre-LN versus Peri-LN).

fits_no_version.finding: An 8B Peri-LN model reached on average 15% lower training loss than an otherwise identical Pre-LN model in the same wall-clock budget, with fewer loss and gradient spikes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalization placement (Peri-LN vs Pre-LN) changes pretraining loss and stability substantially at fixed parameter count.

record.problems: The architecture comparisons cover only a small number of configurations. The normalization comparison reports training loss rather than held-out loss and uses a same-wall-clock comparison; an equal training-token budget is not stated. No uncertainty estimates are given.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying loss outcomes were left out. The reported theoretical compute reduction and increased number of tokens processed are noted in gate_note because they do not measure a claim version's loss outcome.

untested.parts: Shapes other than one depth/width pair (aspect ratios across a wide range, head count, FFN ratio at multiple sizes); equal-token comparison; quantified loss differences.
All: no loss sweep over parameters, tokens or compute.

record.verdict_notes: Industry technical report and preprint. Scaling laws (Kaplan, Chinchilla) are cited in Section 5.1 but not tested. The GPU-hour comparison (Figure 6) and the benchmark tables are not loss measurements. The V4 support rests on a single, number-free sentence.

versions.untested_parts: No loss scaling sweep across parameter count, tokens, or compute.
No small-run fits or predictions of larger-run losses.
No search for loss-minimising parameter and token allocations across compute budgets.

Only a fixed-parameter-count depth/width comparison and a normalization comparison are reported; the latter reports training loss, not held-out loss. Other architecture choices and a wide range of configurations are not tested.
The vision-augmented model is evaluated on a benchmark, but the study does not test whether power-law loss scaling holds in vision or other regimes.
Downstream benchmarks are reported, but no scaling relationship or prediction from pretraining loss is tested.
No comparison of scaling-law fits, exponents, fitting choices, or curve bending.

rows.subject: 3B-parameter shallow-but-wide variant
rows.operation_detail: Reduced depth and increased FFN hidden dimension at a fixed total parameter budget.
rows.baseline: 3B-parameter baseline with 26 Transformer blocks and FFN hidden size 7,168
rows.value: matched the validation perplexity of the deeper control
rows.note: The comparison supports similar modeling quality for this particular depth/width reallocation. The study also says the variant processed 15% more training tokens in the same wall-clock budget, but that is an efficiency result rather than a loss measure.
rows.check: The comparison used an equal wall-clock budget, not equal tokens: the shallow-wide model saw 15% more tokens. Equal per-token loss is therefore not shown. No perplexity numbers or uncertainty are given, and only one shape pair is tested.

rows.subject: 8B-parameter Peri-LN Llama-style model
rows.operation_detail: Compared Peri-LN normalization with an otherwise identical Pre-LN model.
rows.baseline: otherwise identical 8 B-parameter standard Pre-LN model
rows.value: Peri-LN attained, on average, a 15 % lower training loss
rows.note: The text also reports fewer gradient and loss spikes for Peri-LN. It does not state that the comparison used an equal token budget; the loss outcome is training loss, not held-out loss.
rows.check: Pre-LN versus Peri-LN is a change of normalization scheme, not of depth, width or other shape parameters at fixed size, which is what V4 names. The measure is training loss under equal wall-clock and is confounded by Pre-LN loss spikes. It should not be linked to V4.
